Class RunnerJarSpec

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.runner.build.RunnerJarSpec
public final class RunnerJarSpec extends Object
Everything RunnerJarBuilder needs to know to produce a runner jar.

A spec is immutable and is built through builder(). Only the main class, the application output and the output file have to be set; every other option has the default the format was designed around, so the plugins can hand over a spec that mirrors their own conventions without deciding anything the user did not ask about.

RunnerJarSpec spec = RunnerJarSpec.builder()
        .mainClass("com.example.Application")
        .applicationOutput(List.of(classesDir, resourcesDir))
        .dependencies(List.of(new Dependency(nettyJar, "io.netty:netty-common:4.2.1")))
        .output(buildDir.resolve("app-all.jar"))
        .build();

The default timestamp() is 1980-02-01T00:00:00Z, the earliest instant MS-DOS time can represent with a day to spare, and every entry of the archive is dated with it in UTC. That, together with the fixed entry order the builder uses, is what makes two builds of the same inputs produce the same bytes on any machine in any time zone.

Since:
1.0

    • mainClass

      public String mainClass()
      The application main class, in binary form.

      It is recorded in the index and in the Micronaut-Runner-Start-Class manifest attribute, and the build fails when the application output does not contain it.

      Returns:
      the binary class name

    • applicationOutput

      public List<Path> applicationOutput()
      The application's own classes and resources, as directories and jars in the order they take precedence.

      They are packaged exploded under MICRONAUT-INF/classes/ and form jar 0 of the index. When two of them carry the same relative name the first one wins, exactly as it would on a class path, and the build warns about the one that lost.

      Returns:
      the application output, in order

    • applicationManifestSource

      public Optional<Path> applicationManifestSource()
      A jar or MANIFEST.MF file whose attributes describe the application.

      A directory of class files carries no manifest, so this is how the Implementation-Title and friends of the application's own jar reach the runner jar's manifest and the jar 0 record of the index, including its per-package sections.

      Returns:
      the manifest source, if one was configured

    • applicationManifest

      public Optional<Manifest> applicationManifest()
      An already parsed application manifest, as an alternative to applicationManifestSource().

      The returned manifest is a copy; mutating it has no effect on the spec.

      Returns:
      the manifest, if one was configured

    • multiRelease

      public boolean multiRelease()
      Whether the application layer is itself multi-release.

      Only when this is set does the index alias the application's own META-INF/versions/N/... entries; a dependency is aliased when its own manifest says Multi-Release: true, independently of this option.

      Returns:
      whether jar 0 is multi-release

    • entryStub

      public boolean entryStub()
      Whether the generated entry stub was requested.

      A request does not guarantee a stub. The packager generates one only when the main class is a public, non-abstract class in a named package that declares its own public static void main(String[]). When the application layer is declared multi-release, every multi-release variant of that class that the runner can select must have the same directly callable shape. If the request is disabled, a class is ineligible, or the generated class name is already occupied, the packager reports why and leaves the index without a stub; the launcher then uses its reflective fallback.

      Returns:
      whether an entry stub was requested

    • manifestAttributes

      public Map<String,String> manifestAttributes()
      Extra main attributes for the runner jar's manifest.

      They are written after the attributes the format requires and can override the ones taken from the application manifest. Manifest-Version, Main-Class and the entire Micronaut-Runner-* namespace are reserved and rejected case-insensitively because the runner jar format and launcher depend on them.

      Attributes are written in this map's iteration order; pass an ordered map such as LinkedHashMap for byte-for-byte reproducible archives, as both plugins do.

      Returns:
      the extra attributes, in the order they were configured

    • addOpens

      public List<String> addOpens()
      The Add-Opens manifest attribute values.

      Each value uses the JAR manifest grammar module/package; unlike the corresponding Java command-line option, it has no =ALL-UNNAMED suffix.

      Returns:
      the module/package pairs to open, or an empty list

    • addExports

      public List<String> addExports()

      Each value uses the JAR manifest grammar module/package; unlike the corresponding Java command-line option, it has no =ALL-UNNAMED suffix.

      Returns:
      the module/package pairs to export, or an empty list
